clue.text: Where artist has left wine container?

indicators.note: the artist has gone away, so his letters are removed from the container

parts.note: a carafe is a jug for serving wine
RA, a Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter has walked off and abandoned a jug of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Where' is cheeky: a cafe is a place where one might sit; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a place, so it can answer the question word standing for a location.

clue.text: In a strange way an apt clue about old fruit

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for old
the words are arranged strangely, i.e. jumbled

explanation.surface: A peculiar crossword clue about some ancient fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a strange way' rearranges AN APT CLUE, and 'about' puts that round O (old).
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloupe is a variety of melon, a fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Falstaffian wit's no good for a legal ruling

parts.note: Shakespeare's Falstaff is famously fat

indicators.note: the good letter is absent, so it is removed

parts.note: a wag is a witty joker

explanation.surface: Falstaff's jokes are no good as a court verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a recognised authority.

clue.text: Get on after working with English teaching aid

indicators.note: the boarding piece comes after the reworked letters
the letters are put to work, i.e. rearranged into a new order

parts.note: to board a bus or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: Someone climbs aboard after a spell of work with an English class aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' tempts as the definition (succeed), but it is boarding a vehicle; 'working' here is an anagram signal, not employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiteboard is a wipeable classroom board used as a teaching aid.

clue.text: Good time for those not loaded to get loaded

definitions.text: Good time for those not loaded to get loaded

parts.words: Good time for those not loaded to get loaded
parts.note: a time when cheap drinks let people who are not rich (loaded) get drunk (loaded)

explanation.surface: The best moment for the poor to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' is used twice in its two slang senses: rich, then drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy hour is a period when a bar sells drinks cheaply.

clue.text: Pound the beat in month robbery's committed

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A policeman walks the beat in a month when a robbery is committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound the beat' reads as a policeman's patrol; 'the beat' and 'committed' fill out the picture, with THROB itself meaning a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound, of a heart or head, is to beat heavily and rhythmically.

clue.text: God from China almost stopping rise of despicable person

indicators.note: the friend's letters plug the gap inside the other piece
in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a scab is a contemptible person, especially a strike-breaker

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so chum

explanation.surface: A deity emerges from the Far East to halt a villain's advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang (china plate = mate), so CHUM, less its last letter; 'rise of' reverses SCAB to BACS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine.

clue.text: Disclosure in newspaper item on military operation

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement in a newspaper
a mission is a military operation

explanation.surface: A revelation appears in a press report on a military raid.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a confession, the disclosure of something hidden.

clue.text: A little lower

definitions.meaning: a ... is a small amount, as in a ... of milk
to let it fall or lower it

explanation.surface: Slightly reduce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop is both a small quantity of liquid and a verb meaning let down or reduce.

clue.text: Throw away position at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the position word goes first, at the top

parts.note: to put something is to position it
off means away, as in 'run off'

explanation.surface: Discard the place at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, as does to put them off.

clue.text: Some other drink for every deck hand?

parts.note: any drink other than rum is, playfully, 'not rum'
per means for each, as in 'per person'

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck is offered something other than rum, a share each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck hand' suggests a sailor, but the deck is a pack of cards: in bridge a no-trumper is a hand suited to a no-trumps contract.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a hand dealt from the deck that suits playing without trumps is called by this name.

clue.text: Foreign city's entertaining bandleader and jazz group

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Como is a city in northern Italy
the leader, i.e. first letter, of the word band

explanation.surface: An Italian town plays host to a bandleader and a small jazz outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band, especially a jazz group of a few players.

clue.text: Loving what Churchill possibly claimed, but I ignored initially

indicators.note: the I at the very start is overlooked and dropped

parts.note: Winston Churchill, a Conservative leader, might have declared 'I am a Tory'

explanation.surface: An affectionate claim from the wartime prime minister, with the opening word dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill was a British Conservative (Tory) prime minister; drop the I from I AM A TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes things relating to love or lovers, so it means loving.

clue.text: In a flutter, chap is in command

indicators.note: the chap's piece goes in the middle of the wager

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet
chap gives HE, and 'is' joins on as the S of HE'S

explanation.surface: A man in a nervous state happens to be the one giving orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests nerves, but in British usage a flutter is a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest'.

clue.text: Sort of hand dealt out — imagine what follows

indicators.note: like cards dealt out, the letters are distributed in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of card hand is dealt, and you can guess the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means et cetera, inviting the reader to supply what comes next.

clue.text: Where agent usually gets money from is not working

definitions.text: Where agent usually gets money from
definitions.meaning: an agent's pay usually comes from a percentage cut of each deal
a broken machine or idle ship is not in service

explanation.surface: An agent paid on percentage is out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means taken from a percentage cut, and idiomatically means not in working order.

clue.text: Snake in the grass picked up by boy wearing hat

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up raises the word, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a rat, like a snake in the grass, is a treacherous person
Paul is a boy's name
if you are in a coat you are wearing it

explanation.surface: A snake in the grass is lifted by a lad in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses RAT to TAR. 'Snake in the grass' suggests a serpent but means a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin was a sailor's hat made of tarred cloth.

clue.text: Traffic warden giving report of distance travelled?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a metre is a distance and 'made' means travelled, as in 'made ten miles'

explanation.surface: A parking officer giving an account of a journey's length.
explanation.walkthrough: METRE MADE (distance travelled) sounds like METER MAID; 'report of' marks the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Meter maid is an informal name for a female traffic warden who checks parking meters.

clue.text: Rag prints shock in new revelation about cold bar snack

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the abbreviation for cold
the letters are revealed anew, rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A tabloid publishes a shocking exposé about a chilled pub nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new revelation' rearranges RAG PRINTS SHOCK, and 'about' wraps that round C (cold).
explanation.definitionFit: Pork scratchings are crunchy fried pork rind, a classic British pub snack served at the bar.

clue.text: Place in Washington Square's surrounding area

indicators.note: the square's letters go round the abbreviation for area

parts.note: to square a debt is to settle it

explanation.surface: A city plaza encircles a district in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington Square' looks like the New York park; Washington here is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in the US state of Washington.

clue.text: Take place of guillotined man, a writer

indicators.note: the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a chap is a man
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Taking the place of a beheaded man and a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take place of' looks like 'replace', but 'Take place' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen is to occur, i.e. to take place.

clue.text: Varnishes very good for Viennese vessels

parts.note: ja, German for yes, is how a Viennese speaker says 'very good' in agreement
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A Viennese approves of some cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a hard glossy black lacquer, and to japan something is to varnish it; plural verb to match.

clue.text: Ropemaker's thrown up short rope I caught

indicators.note: in a down clue thrown up means read upwards, i.e. backwards
the I is caught inside the shortened rope
a rope cut short loses its final letter, so the word is trimmed at its end

parts.note: a lasso is a rope with a noose

explanation.surface: A rope-maker has been sick after catching a bit of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: LASSO shortened is LASS; 'caught' puts I inside to give LASIS, which 'thrown up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is the plant fibre a rope-maker uses; the 's reads as 'is', a rope-maker's material.

clue.text: Criticism of evidence given by soldiers at front

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters are placed before the evidence

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are a British army corps
proof is evidence that establishes a fact

explanation.surface: Troops on the front line give evidence that draws criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or expression of disapproval.

clue.text: Difficult, having little time at the end to make anything at all

indicators.note: the time letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: tough means difficult
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It's hard, with little time left, to make anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having little time at the end' moves T (time) from the front of TOUGH to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old variant of aught, meaning anything at all.

clue.text: Bike found in courtyard

definitions.meaning: a ... bike is a four-wheeled motorbike, called a ... for short
a ... (quadrangle) is a courtyard, as in a college

explanation.surface: A motorbike turns up in a college yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Quad is short both for quad bike and for quadrangle, an enclosed courtyard.

clue.text: In the dark? Not if one's succeeded before

parts.words: In the dark? Not if one's succeeded before
parts.note: something never set alight; if someone had managed to light it earlier, it would no longer be so

explanation.surface: Ignorant? Not if you have already done well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the dark' reads as ignorant; the second half shows it means not set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left without light or flame is in the dark, literally unilluminated.

clue.text: Refuse to be picked up by such a person

definitions.text: Refuse to be picked up by such a person

parts.words: Refuse to be picked up by such a person
parts.note: read 'refuse' as the noun rubbish, which such a person collects

explanation.surface: Declining to be given a lift by this sort of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline), but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger collects discarded things, picking through rubbish.

clue.text: Scholars may thank her for helping or just scoff

definitions.text: Scholars may thank her for helping or just scoff

parts.words: Scholars may thank her for helping or just scoff
parts.note: schoolchildren (scholars) receive a helping of lunch from her, and may either thank her or simply eat it

explanation.surface: Students may be grateful for her assistance or sneer at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' is a serving of food and 'scoff' means to eat greedily, not to mock; British school lunches are served by these staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner lady is a woman who serves midday meals in a British school.

clue.text: State of top-class bowler's spinning

parts.note: U, as in upper-class usage, means top-class

indicators.note: the hat spins round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a bowler is a hat; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A first-rate cricket bowler is spinning the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but it is the hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.
